To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the power-law exponent is given by the sum of the exponent of the dispersion function and the reaction order, the dispersion parameter can be expressed as a function of the reaction rate, and the saturation behavior is governed by the dispersion function.

(1) dispersive transport models for NBTI can be divided into two groups, one where hydrogen transport is assumed to be trap-controlled, the other one where it is trap-limited, (2) for the trap-controlled case, the time exponent in the power-law dependence of the threshold voltage shift on stress time depends on both the initial conditions and the boundary conditions, and (3) the trap-limited case is a special case of the trap-controlled case with specific boundary conditions.

(i) the time exponent is always reduced by dispersive transport, but the magnitude of the reduction is dependent on the initial and boundary conditions; (ii) the prefactor of the power law is always reduced; and (iii) the saturation behavior is always reduced.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of models for dispersive transport and NBTI.
the development of a generalized reaction-dispersive diffusion formalism for NBTI, and the clarification of the discrepancies between the various published NBTI models.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all models are correct in the limit that the dispersion parameter goes to zero, i.e., in the absence of dispersive transport.
, in the absence of a detailed microscopic model, the time evolution of the NBTI threshold-voltage shift is determined by the initial and boundary conditions.
the power-law time-exponent is not a unique function of the dispersion parameter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NBTI reaction-diffusion models are all based on a common physical assumption, but the different models are based on different assumptions about the initial and boundary conditions.
the dispersive transport models can be classified into two categories.
dispersive transport is a viable approach for NBTI modeling, but that care must be taken when interpreting the dispersion parameter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the boundary conditions are the crucial element in determining the power-law time exponents and their dependence on the dispersion parameter.
the initial and boundary conditions are not uniquely determined by the physical assumptions.
the dispersive diffusion equation must be coupled to a reaction at the interface.
